observed_launcher_behavior: The G2 launcher explicitly pins piper-tts==1.7.0, numpy==1.26.4 and soundfile==0.13.1 but does not explicitly pin onnxruntime in the pip command.

external_primary_evidence.observation: Current official Piper Python packaging declares onnxruntime>=1,<2 as an install dependency and packages an embedded espeak bridge/data inside the Piper distribution.

PiperVoice.load/synthesize uses the Python inference path; CUDA mode explicitly swaps to onnxruntime-gpu, demonstrating that the ONNX Runtime provider/runtime is a material inference dependency rather than interpreter identity.
piper-tts 1.7.0 is the exact package version requested by the current G2 launcher.

finding.reason: A deterministic manifest of only the piper-tts distribution does not cover the separately installed onnxruntime distribution/native shared libraries/execution provider used for ONNX inference. The same Piper package/model/interpreter can execute through a different allowed ONNX Runtime 1.x build or provider.
finding.false_green_risk: Terminal TTS runtime identity could remain unchanged while the inference engine that generated the bound WAV changed, weakening exact waveform-runtime lineage.
finding.scope: Refinement of existing TTS_RUNTIME_IDENTITY blocker; do not create a seventh independent terminal blocker.

minimal_trigger4_repair_precision: Record deterministic piper-tts distribution manifest SHA256 including its embedded espeak bridge/data used by the installed wheel.
Record exact installed onnxruntime distribution version and deterministic distribution manifest SHA256.

Resolve and hash the actual loaded ONNX Runtime native shared library/libraries where deterministically available; record the active execution provider list from the exact Piper session. For current use_cuda=False the expected provider should be CPU, but verify observed provider rather than infer it.
Keep Python executable hash as auxiliary interpreter identity, not canonical TTS runtime identity.
Bind piper manifest + ONNX Runtime manifest/native identity + provider + model/config hashes + source text + generated WAV hash into the same packet_audio_binding/source lineage.

If a material native inference dependency cannot be deterministically resolved, terminal guard must fail closed as EVIDENCE_INVALID_TTS_RUNTIME_IDENTITY rather than silently falling back to interpreter identity.

reproducibility_preference.preferred: Pin the exact ONNX Runtime version used by the G2 S2 launcher in addition to recording its exact installed manifest/native identity, so future fresh S2 subjects do not silently resolve a different allowed 1.x dependency.
reproducibility_preference.why_record_even_when_pinned: Version pins are selection policy, not proof of installed bytes; terminal evidence still needs observed runtime identity.

focused_regressions: Same piper-tts manifest/model/interpreter with two synthetic onnxruntime manifests must produce different canonical TTS runtime identities.
Missing onnxruntime identity/provider with otherwise complete Piper/model hashes must make terminal required-observables incomplete.
Changing only Python interpreter path/hash while keeping exact Piper+ONNX native runtime unchanged must not masquerade as a TTS engine change; interpreter remains separately observable.
Observed provider/runtime identity must be bound to both old and replacement waveform generation lineage or an explicitly shared generation-session identity.
next_action: Trigger4 folds this into the existing TTS_RUNTIME_IDENTITY repair inside the one six-blocker descendant; no separate generation or authority.
